Hakkoz
HAK-koz
proper noun
Hebrew haqqots, “the thorn” or “the nimble,” the head of the seventh of the four and twenty courses of the priests appointed by David.

Biblical Definition

Hakkoz is named as the head of the seventh course of the priests, the chief to whom the seventh lot came forth when David ordered the sons of Aaron into their courses for the house of the LORD (1Ch 24:10). His name signifies “the thorn,” and a solemn providence attends his house, for in the days of Ezra the children of Koz were among those who sought their register among them that were reckoned by genealogy, and it was not found; therefore were they, as polluted, put from the priesthood (Ezr 2:61-62). The Tirshatha forbade them the most holy things until there stood up a priest with Urim and with Thummim. Yet the LORD did not utterly cast off the house, for Meremoth the son of Urijah the son of Koz wrought faithfully upon the wall under Nehemiah (Neh 3:4,21). The dictionary marks the weight of this: the priesthood of Aaron rested upon a sure register, and he that could not prove his descent might not minister at the altar. There is a sober gospel here, for our acceptance before God rests not upon a genealogy we cannot keep, but upon the High Priest after the order of Melchisedec, who is made priest, not after the law of a carnal commandment, but after the power of an endless life. Hakkoz stands as a witness that the old priesthood was bound to the flesh and could fail, but the priesthood of Christ abideth for ever.

Webster 1828 Definition

The head of the seventh course of the priests, whose descendants in Ezra’s day could not prove their priestly genealogy.

HAKKOZ, the head of the seventh course of the priests, signifying “the thorn.”

The seventh lot came forth to him when David ordered the sons of Aaron.

His descendants, the children of Koz, could not find their register in Ezra’s day.

They were put from the priesthood as polluted, till a priest should stand with Urim and Thummim.

Yet Meremoth of the sons of Koz wrought faithfully upon the wall under Nehemiah.

Key Scripture

1Ch 24:10 — "The seventh to Hakkoz, the eighth to Abijah,"

Ezr 2:62 — "These sought their register among those that were reckoned by genealogy, but they were not found: therefore were they, as polluted, put from the priesthood."

Neh 3:4 — "And next unto them repaired Meremoth the son of Urijah, the son of Koz. And next unto them repaired Meshullam the son of Berechiah, the son of Meshezabeel. And next unto them repaired Zadok the son of Baana."

Heb 7:16 — "Who is made, not after the law of a carnal commandment, but after the power of an endless life."

Modern Corruption

A name of Scripture, not a contested doctrine; it witnesses to a priesthood bound to the flesh that could fail, and to the abiding priesthood of Christ.

expand to see more

Hakkoz is a name of the sacred record of the courses, and no movement of the present age has troubled itself to redefine it. The dictionary records it that the reader who meets the name at the head of the seventh course may mark the sober history of his house, whose register was lost and whose sons were for a time put from the priesthood.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that the priesthood of Aaron was bound to the flesh and to a register that might be lost, but the priesthood of Christ is after the power of an endless life. He who put the children of Koz from the altar for want of a genealogy is the same who hath given us a High Priest whose descent we need not prove, for He is made priest by the oath of God for ever. The saint who trembles at his own unworthiness may remember Hakkoz, and rest not in any record of his own, but in the unchangeable priesthood of the Son of God.

Hebrew Roots

From the Hebrew for “the thorn,” Hakkoz names the head of the seventh priestly course.
